stories.title: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario 'Lake America' amid rising trade tensions with Canada
stories.summary: Donald Trump has signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" in the US, as his administration's trade dispute with neighbouring Canada intensifies. US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he would rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" in the United States, as his trade dispute with Canada intensifies. The Republican president signed an executive order directing the US agency responsible for geographic names to update the lake's name. The order applies only in the United States, meaning Trump cannot require Canada to adopt the new name. The move echoes Trump's decision last year to rename the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America". Trump signed the order at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office, with a large map of the Great Lakes displayed behind him. The words "Lake America" appeared in large red letters over Lake Ontario. Speaking to reporters, Trump described Canada as "the worst" country to deal with on trade. "They think they are entitled to everything and we cannot allow it," he said. The announcement comes amid escalating trade tensions between Washington and Ottawa, after the United States announced 50% tariffs on around $20 billion (€17.17 billion) worth of Canadian goods following the collapse of negotiations between the two countries. Trump has repeatedly increased pressure on the United States' northern neighbour since returning to the White House last year. He has also suggested that Canada, a longstanding US ally, should become the country's 51st state.

stories.title: Russian, US intel chiefs on good terms, talk regularly — Trump
stories.summary: The US president downplayed Ratcliffe’s recent trip to Moscow, calling it "routine"
article_sentences: WASHINGTON, August 27.

Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) Director John Ratcliffe and Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) head Sergey Naryshkin get on well and hold regular talks, said US President Donald Trump in an interview with Axios portal.
He downplayed Ratcliffe’s recent trip to Moscow, calling it "routine," adding he was puzzled about the media hoopla surrounding it.
"Ratcliffe sees his Russian counterpart once every six months or once every year.
They have a very good relationship.
There was no message and there was nothing unusual," Trump said.

stories.title: US Open men’s draw pits Russian Safiullin against defending champ Alcaraz in opener
stories.summary: Andrey Rublev will begin the tourney against Croatia’s Marin Cilic
article_sentences: NEW YORK, August 27.
Russian tennis player Roman Safiullin will play in round one of the 2026 US Open, which kicks off this Sunday, against World No.
3 and defending champ Carlos Alcaraz from Spain, according to the men’s draw which was revealed on Thursday.
Three other Russian men are also playing at this year’s closing Grand Slam tournament.
Russia’s top male racquet.

Daniil Medvedev will play in the opening round against an as-yet unknown qualifier, Andrey Rublev will begin the tourney against Croatia’s Marin Cilic and Karen Khachanov will face off against Roman Burruchaga from Argentina in the opening round.
The 2026 US Open is played on outdoor hard courts at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in New York between August 30 and September 13.
The tournament will award $90 million in prize money.
Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz is the tournament’s reigning champion.
Russian tennis players are participating in international tournaments under a neutral status and the US Open is no exception.

On February 28, 2022, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) issued recommendations to international sports federations to bar athletes from Russia and Belarus from taking part in international tournaments, citing Moscow's special military operation in Ukraine as the reason.
Following the IOC's recommendations in late February 2022, the majority of global sports federations moved to exclude athletes from Russia and Belarus from all international sports tournaments.
